tier_reason: The record's tegridy-benchie RESULTS.md numbers match the native simd-json (rust) and serde_json rows, and the harness is public (rust/simdjson.rs, rust/serde.rs, rust/runner.rs, Cargo release profile opt-level=3, lto, codegen-units=1, CPU i7-6820HQ), so it already meets A without a rustc version. A stronger A source is serde-rs/json-benchmark (src/main.rs, .cargo/config target-cpu=native, rustc 1.59.0-nightly 2021-12-07, i7-6600U), a known benchmark run by serde's own author, so benchmark_url now points there.

corrections.claimed_speedup: DOM parse: canada.json 380 vs serde_json 320 MB/s (~1.19x), citm_catalog.json 720 vs 420 MB/s (~1.71x), twitter.json 810 vs 300 MB/s (~2.7x); struct parse: canada.json 580 vs 580 MB/s (1.0x), citm_catalog.json 1220 vs 710 MB/s (~1.72x), twitter.json 1050 vs 550 MB/s (~1.91x) (ratios derived from page data)
corrections.workload: serde-rs/json-benchmark, a Rust port of nativejson-benchmark: in-memory parse to DOM (simd-json BorrowedValue vs serde_json Value), parse to typed structs, and DOM stringify of canada.json, citm_catalog.json and twitter.json; the best of 256 trials is kept, and the README takes the better of two runs
corrections.compiler_and_flags: rustc 1.59.0-nightly (0b6f079e4 2021-12-07); cargo run --release with RUSTFLAGS -C target-cpu=native (.cargo/config); release profile debug=true, panic=abort; jemalloc global allocator
corrections.caveats: The json-benchmark numbers date from 2021-12-08 and use simd-json 0.4.11 and serde_json 1.0.72. The Cargo.toml that matches them is at commit c8bf3ee. The repo is archived (last push 2024-03-26), later crate bumps to simd-json 0.12 were never re-run, and simd-json is now at 0.18.1. DOM stringify is mixed: 470 vs 430, 760 vs 560, and 890 vs 910 MB/s, so simd-json is slower on twitter.json. Struct parse ties on canada.json. A recent real-workload shootout (mihailnica10/tegridy-benchie RESULTS.md, generated 2026-09-23, 0 stars, single commit) shows only near parity. That run uses simd-json 0.13.11 with runtime detection and no target-cpu=native, OwnedValue plus a buffer copy, and a fused fact-reduction step. Its results are 115.2 vs 104.3 MB/s at 8 threads (~1.10x), 50.6 vs 48.0 MB/s at 1 thread (~1.05x), and ~1.01x at 2 and 4 threads. serde_json is slightly ahead in its Bun 8-worker FFI pool (124.5 vs 123.0 MB/s). simd-json's own README has only a qualitative performance claim and no numbers. Good results need AVX2/SSE4.2/NEON, and the parser mutates its input buffer.

notes: The record was accurate: the tegridy-benchie numbers belong to the simd-json (rust) rows. The tegridy real-workload margin (~1.0-1.1x) is kept in caveats. The license is dual MIT OR Apache-2.0 per the README and the LICENSE-MIT/LICENSE-APACHE files (the gh API reports only Apache-2.0). tier_reason: The README Benchmarks block runs Sonic against encoding/json (StdLib rows) and states goversion 1.17.1 and the CPU (i9-9880H, darwin/amd64). The code is public: encoder/encoder_test.go, decoder/decoder_test.go, and external_jsonlib_test/benchmark_test/*, driven by scripts/bench.sh with go test -benchmem -benchtime=100000x. With code, compiler, flags and CPU all stated, the tier is A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: BenchmarkEncoder_Generic_Sonic 32393 ns/op vs StdLib 106322 ns/op (~3.3x); BenchmarkDecoder_Generic_Sonic 66812 ns/op vs StdLib 124260 ns/op (~1.9x); BenchmarkDecoder_Binding_Sonic 32557 ns/op vs StdLib 111437 ns/op (~3.4x); BenchmarkEncoder_Parallel_Binding_Sonic 8810.09 MB/s vs StdLib 3486.49 MB/s (~2.5x), or 10785.23 MB/s (~3.1x) with Sonic_Fast options (derived from page data)
corrections.caveats: The README benchmark uses an old Go toolchain (1.17.1) on one Mac laptop, and current sonic requires Go 1.18-1.27. The *_Fast rows drop SortMapKeys/EscapeHTML (NoQuoteTextMarshaler), so they are not like-for-like with encoding/json. The std-option Sonic rows are the fair comparison. Sonic is JIT/assembly-based for amd64 and arm64 (arm64 needs go1.20+). On unsupported environments it falls back to encoding/json. A third-party real-workload shootout (mihailnica10/tegridy-benchie RESULTS.md, 2026-09-23, 0 stars, single commit, sonic v1.15.4, go.mod go 1.27.1, i7-6820HQ) corroborates a ~1.8-2.0x native win over encoding/json on a 39.9MB SEC company-facts corpus. Its figures are 86.1 vs 44.5 MB/s at 1 thread, 180.2 vs 100.7 at 4 threads, and 260.0 vs 128.8 at 8 threads, and ~1.7x via Bun FFI (73.2 vs 42.5 MB/s) (derived). In that shootout sonic trails goccy/go-json at 1-4 threads.

notes: The README numbers match exactly, and the Generic Sonic encoder benchmark uses std-equivalent options (SortMapKeys|EscapeHTML). tier_reason: The README tables compare zzzjson with RapidJSON (plus rapidjsonfp and rapidjsonstr) and 8 other C/C++ libraries, and state the CPU (i7-6700 3.40GHz), compiler (G++-7.3) and optimization (O3). corrections.claimed_speedup: 'All JSON Above' total time 166ms (zzzjson) vs 220ms (RapidJSON) (~1.33x); Random Short JSON 38ms vs 56ms (~1.47x); Random Long JSON 29ms vs 45ms (~1.55x); No-Number JSON 149ms vs 224ms (~1.50x); JSON From Taobao 23ms vs 28ms (~1.22x); JSON From nativejson-benchmark 22ms vs 23ms (~1.05x, parity; parse alone 18ms vs 11ms, slower) (derived from page data)
corrections.workload: Parse, stringify and parse+stringify ('All') wall time (ms) in memory over no-number JSON (nonum*.json), nativejson-benchmark files (canada, citm_catalog, twitter), Taobao JSON (cart, trade), all of these plus json-iterator large-file.json, and random short/long JSON, run via build.sh all
corrections.license: Public Domain (custom dedication in LICENSE: 'zzzjson is public domain. Do whatever you want with it.'; not a formal OSI/SPDX license)
corrections.caveats: The numbers are 2018-2019 era (the README tables were last touched 2019-04-18) and come from GCC 7.3 on Ubuntu 18.04 under WSL. The repository has had no commits since 2020-12-26. Most of the win is in stringify: parse alone is at parity (95 vs 97ms on All JSON) or slower (18 vs 11ms on the nativejson-benchmark files). zzzJSON's 'parse on use' keeps numbers as text and does not convert them, while RapidJSON (kParseDefaultFlags) converts numbers, so the comparison is not like-for-like on number-heavy data. The 'All' column is timed separately and does not always equal parse plus stringify. Newer leaders (yyjson, simdjson) are not in the comparison. The LICENSE is an informal public-domain dedication with no SPDX id and grants no patent rights.
